claims.text: Ninety-seven percent of children and adolescents in the United States play video games for at least one hour per day.
Playing video games yields positive effects in the cognitive domain.
Playing video games yields positive effects in the motivational domain.
Playing video games yields positive effects in the emotional domain.
Playing video games yields positive effects in the social domain.

evidence.description: 97% playing for at least one hour per day in the United States.
A small but significant body of research emerging mostly in the last five years documents these benefits.

methodologies.name: Theoretical synthesis and literature review
methodologies.description: Summarizes research on the positive effects of gaming across four main domains and integrates theoretical insights from developmental, positive, social, and media psychology.

limitations.text: The vast majority of psychological research on gaming has focused predominantly on negative impacts related to violence, addiction, and depression.
The mental health benefits of gaming remain largely unexplored.

future_work.text: Establish new programs of research focused on the mental health benefits of gaming.
Conduct intervention research and clinical applications to test the positive uses of video games.
